title: Pork Schnitzel with Buttered Noodles
subtitle: thin, crisp golden pork cutlets with lemon, over buttery egg noodles
imageAlt: A large golden breaded pork cutlet with lemon wedges beside buttered egg noodles on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Pound the chops thin and even (5 mm) between plastic wrap; they cook in minutes and stay tender.
Start the noodle water before you bread the pork.

steps.title: Water on
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.

steps.title: Pound
steps.text: Pound the chops between sheets of plastic wrap to 5 mm thick. Season both sides with the salt, pepper and paprika.

steps.title: Bread
steps.text: Put the flour in one shallow dish, the eggs beaten with the milk in another and the panko in a third. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high until a crumb sizzles. Fry 2 cutlets at a time 2–3 minutes a side, until deep golden and 71°C (160°F). Drain on a rack and keep warm in a 95°C (200°F) oven.

steps.title: Noodles
steps.text: Meanwhile, cook the noodles 6–8 minutes until tender, drain and toss with the butter.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the schnitzel on the noodles with lemon wedges to squeeze over.

fixIt.fix: Pat the pork dry first and don't move the cutlets for the first minute in the oil.
The oil wasn't hot enough. Wait until a crumb sizzles hard before adding the pork.
Lower to medium; thin cutlets cook through in the time it takes to brown.

saleTip: Boneless pork chops are among the cheapest No Frills meats on sale; pounding them makes 4 chops feel like a feast.
swap: Chicken breasts: halve them horizontally and pound to 5 mm; fry to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Slice into a sandwich on a toasted bun with mayo and lettuce.
doneness: 71°C (160°F) in the centre (Health Canada, pork). Thin cutlets get there in 2–3 minutes a side.
source: Based on tested schnitzel methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): pork pounded to 5 mm, breaded flour-egg-crumb and shallow-fried in hot oil, served with lemon.
prepAhead: Pound and bread the cutlets up to 4 hours ahead; keep uncovered on a rack in the fridge.
reheat: Air fryer or oven at 200°C (400°F) 5–6 minutes, until 74°C (165°F) and crisp.

basic.note: Salt and pepper on the pork, plain buttered noodles.

stepNotes.2: Basic: beat the eggs on their own.

fancy.note: A creamy pan sauce (rahmschnitzel) spooned over.

addSteps.title: Cream sauce
addSteps.text: Pour the oil out of the skillet and wipe it. Simmer the broth 2 minutes, add the cream and simmer 2–3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir in the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, and spoon beside the schnitzel.

plating: Schnitzel overlapping the noodles, not on top.
Sauce spooned beside so the crust stays crisp.

why.0-0: Pounding thin means fast cooking, so the crust browns just as the pork is done.
why.0-6: A spoon of milk loosens the egg so it coats thinly and evenly.

funFact: Wiener Schnitzel must be veal by Austrian law; made with pork, it's 'Schnitzel Wiener Art', Viennese-style.

keeps.note: freeze fried cutlets flat; re-crisp in the oven

airFryer: Air-fry the breaded cutlets in one layer at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and 71°C (160°F). Lightly spray or brush the coating with oil first so it browns.
drink: A crisp lager or a dry Riesling, or sparkling apple juice.
